wtp:wtp-7VYA1R.description: **You're being attacked! Do you have a way to kill all of your opponent's creatures without losing any of yours?**

fields.name: Board
fields.value: Battle phase · Your turn · Opponent has initiative

wtp:wtp-7VYA1R.title: 🧩 Metal Blowout

wtp:wtp-7VYA1R:solution.description:
Start by activating Soul Reaver twice. First, remove 2 counters from it to kill their 2/2 (either one works). Then, remove 1 counter from it to kill their 1/1. This leaves 1 counter, making Soul Reaver a 3/4. Each of those creatures dying triggers Refuse Reclaimer, adding two +1/+1 counters.

Then go to blocks. Block their 3/3 with Soul Reaver, block their remaining 2/2 with your (now 3/3) Refuse Reclaimer and put your Cosmic Consirator blocking their very large Aether Channeler.

Before damage, virus Trashling onto Cosmic Consirator that's blocking the Aether Channeler, giving it Unaware, which means it ignores the +1/+1 counters and treats it as a 2/3.

Your creatures are all larger than theirs! Congratulations :)
wtp:wtp-7VYA1R:solution.title: 🔑 Metal Blowout — the answer

wtp:wtp-BLOCKD.description: **You attacked, they've declared their block, and nobody has anything left to play. They're at 9. Are they dead?**

fields.name: Board
fields.value: Battle phase · Your turn · You have initiative

fields.name: Notes
fields.value: Blocks are locked in. Count it up before you look.

footer.text: wtp-BLOCKD · easy · combat math · lethal · by Bena

wtp:wtp-BLOCKD.title: 🧩 Is it lethal?

wtp:wtp-BLOCKD:solution.description:
**Yes — exactly lethal.** They take **9** and they're at 9.

The trap is column 1. Once a defending unit is placed in front of an attacking column, **that entire column is blocked, and blocked units deal no combat damage to you**. Tidal Menace's 7 power goes into Cosmic Conspirator, not into their face. It contributes **0** to the kill.

What actually gets through:
- **Column 2** — unblocked: Eldritch Reclaimer (4) + Delver of Mysteries (2) = **6**
- **Column 3** — unblocked: Lonely Forager = **3**

**6 + 3 = 9.** They're at 9. Dead, exactly.

(Column 1 still resolves on the side: Tidal Menace deals 7 to Cosmic Conspirator (3/3), which dies; the 4 excess has no back row to spill into and does *not* carry on to the player. Conspirator deals 3 back into your 7/2 Tidal Menace, which dies. An even trade, and irrelevant to whether they're dead.)
wtp:wtp-BLOCKD:solution.title: 🔑 Is it lethal? — the answer

wtp:wtp-COLUMN.description: **They're swinging with both columns and you're at 5 life. You have one blocker. Which column do you block — and do you live?**

fields.name: Board
fields.value: Battle phase · Opponent's turn · Opponent has initiative

fields.name: Notes
fields.value: Blocks aren't declared yet. Nobody has any tricks — this is pure math.

footer.text: wtp-COLUMN · easy · combat math · blocking · by Bena

wtp:wtp-COLUMN.title: 🧩 Read the whole column

wtp:wtp-COLUMN:solution.description:
**Block column 1.** You end the turn at 2 life, and you kill both of their units.

Column 1 is not a 2/2. **A column deals damage equal to the combined power of every unit in it**, so column 1 is Tiderunner Initiate (2) + Dreadwave Devourer (6) = **8 power**. Column 2 is **3**.

You're at 5:
- Block column 2 → column 1 hits you for **8** → you're dead.
- Block column 1 → column 2 hits you for **3** → you're at **2**. Alive.

And the block is a blowout. Tidal Menace deals **7** into column 1, and damage runs **front to back**: Tiderunner Initiate (2/2) takes 2 and dies, and the **5 excess carries to the back row**, where Dreadwave Devourer (6/4) takes 5 and dies too. Excess beyond the back row does *not* carry on to you — that would need Piercing.

So you trade a 7/2 for a 2/2 *and* a 6/4, and you survive. Tidal Menace dies (column 1 deals 8 into its 2 toughness), but that's a bargain.
wtp:wtp-COLUMN:solution.title: 🔑 Read the whole column — the answer

wtp:wtp-KPGT88.description: **You're being attacked! How should you block and counter attack?**

fields.name: Board
fields.value: Battle phase · Your turn · Opponent has initiative

wtp:wtp-KPGT88.title: 🧩 Blocking Practice

wtp:wtp-KPGT88:solution.description:
Block the first column with your 2/2 flying Drifter, it's the only creature that can block the column. Then block their 2/2 Generic unit with your 1/1. And declare that your Rook is counter attacking. Leave the 3/3 unblocked.

Before damage, virus your Colossus onto their 3/3 deadly unit. That will make your units much stronger. 

Your 2/2 flyer becomes a 4/4 and kills their entire flying column (and survices). And your now 3/3 Generic unit eats their 2/2.

Then, when you attack, your 6/6 Rook will deal them 6 damage and you win the game!
wtp:wtp-KPGT88:solution.title: 🔑 Blocking Practice — the answer

wtp:wtp-SPILL.description: **Blocks are locked and combat damage is about to happen. Which of these four units survive?**

fields.name: Board
fields.value: Battle phase · Opponent's turn · Opponent has initiative

fields.name: Notes
fields.value: No tricks, no attributes in play — just work the damage through.

footer.text: wtp-SPILL · easy · combat math · damage · by Bena

wtp:wtp-SPILL.title: 🧩 Who's left standing?

wtp:wtp-SPILL:solution.description:
**None of them.** All four units die. Everything happens **simultaneously**, so nobody gets to fight back — work each column's damage through separately.

**Their column deals 10** (Tidal Menace 7 + Lonely Forager 3) into your column:
- Cosmic Conspirator (3/3) takes 3 → **dies**
- the **7 excess carries to the back row** → Perpetual Construct (1/3) takes 7 → **dies**

**Your column deals 4** (Cosmic Conspirator 3 + Perpetual Construct 1) into theirs:
- Tidal Menace is a 7/2 — it only has **2 toughness**. It takes 2 → **dies**
- the **2 excess carries to the back row** → Lonely Forager (3/1) takes 2 → **dies**

That's the lesson: a 7/2 hits like a truck and dies to a stiff breeze, and a column with only 4 power still wipes a column of 10 power's worth of stats, because damage spills front to back and both of their units are made of paper.

(Excess beyond the *back* row is where it stops — it does not carry on to the player. That would need Piercing.)
wtp:wtp-SPILL:solution.title: 🔑 Who's left standing? — the answer

wtp:wtp-TOKENS.description: **Blocks aren't declared yet. That 6/6 is the problem — can you kill it this combat, and how do you set your blocking formation?**

fields.name: Board
fields.value: Battle phase · Opponent's turn · Opponent has initiative

fields.name: Notes
fields.value: Everything on this board is a token, so there's no card text anywhere — it really is just the numbers. Your three units are in play but not yet in formation.

footer.text: wtp-TOKENS · medium · combat math · blocking · tokens · by Bena

wtp:wtp-TOKENS.title: 🧩 Stack the blockers

wtp:wtp-TOKENS:solution.description:
**Yes. Put both Robots in one column, in front of theirs.** The 6/6 dies.

The rule that a column deals **combined power** isn't just an attacking rule — **a defending column sums too**. So:

- One Robot blocking alone deals **3**. The 6/6 shrugs it off.
- **Both Robots stacked in the same column** (one front, one back) deal **3 + 3 = 6** — exactly enough to kill a 6/6.

Damage into their column runs front to back, so all 6 lands on Generic Unit 6/6 and kills it. There's **no excess**, so the Robot 3 behind it walks away untouched.

What it costs you: their column deals **9** (6 + 3) into your blocking column. Your front Robot (3/3) takes 3 and dies, and the **6 excess carries to the back Robot** (3/3), which dies too. So you trade **both 3/3s for their 6/6** and take **0** damage.

Your Generic Unit 2/2 stays out of it — a column is only ever **two deep**, so it can't join the stack, and throwing it in front of nothing achieves nothing.
wtp:wtp-TOKENS:solution.title: 🔑 Stack the blockers — the answer
